sections.title: Read the monthly allowance in the right unit
paragraphs:
Abby offers human receptionists, AI answering or a combination. Its current monthly plans are shown below. These are dated published prices, not a promise about your final invoice. The pricing page describes month-to-month service; do not treat these amounts as an annual prepayment offer or assume an unpublished annual discount.

| Plan | Monthly subscription | Included Abby Minutes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starter | $164 | 50 |
| Essential | $329 | 100 |
| Professional | $599 | 200 |
| Growth | $1,380 | 500 |

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [Abby: current pricing](https://www.abby.com/pricing/).

sections.title: Calculate the mix before estimating overage
paragraphs:
One measured human minute consumes one Abby Minute; one measured AI minute consumes half. A call using both is split by the portion each handles. This gives an office a meaningful option when some calls require people and others can follow an AI workflow.

For the following original example, assume the times are already billable measured minutes after the applicable timing rules. They are fictional workloads, not observed customer performance.

| Fictional monthly workload | Calculation | Abby Minutes consumed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 human minutes + 40 AI minutes | 30 + (40 ÷ 2) | 50 |
| 10 human minutes + 80 AI minutes | 10 + (80 ÷ 2) | 50 |
| 45 human minutes + 30 AI minutes | 45 + (30 ÷ 2) | 60 |

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [Abby: terms and conditions](https://www.abby.com/resources/terms-and-conditions/), [Abby: Human + AI receptionist](https://www.abby.com/human-ai-receptionist/).

sections.title: Use the published overage rate, not base-price division
paragraphs:
Abby’s terms list overage at $3.29 per Abby Minute for Starter and Essential, $2.99 for Professional and $2.76 for Growth. Dividing a subscription price by its allowance is not the contractual overage calculation.

Under the fictional 60-Abby-Minute Starter case above, 10 extra units at $3.29 add $32.90 to $164, giving $196.90 before taxes or other applicable charges. That arithmetic does not establish your call mix, every billable activity or an invoice quote.

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [Abby: terms and conditions](https://www.abby.com/resources/terms-and-conditions/).

sections.title: Check how recorded time becomes measured time
paragraphs:
The terms include ring, talk and transfer time, exclude potential hold time, and describe two rounding steps: each included component goes up to a whole second; their total then goes up to a 30-second mark. Raw conversation duration therefore is not enough to recreate usage.

Ask Abby to explain a sample usage record for your proposed arrangement. Have the example identify which part was human, which was AI, the included timing components and the resulting units. If a busy-month forecast approaches a plan boundary, request both a normal-month and a peak-month estimate using the same assumptions.

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [Abby: terms and conditions](https://www.abby.com/resources/terms-and-conditions/).

sections.title: Decide where human handling is worth purchasing
paragraphs:
Start with the work rather than assuming every minute is interchangeable. A contractor might want a person to handle an existing-customer exception while using AI for a straightforward new request. Write which decisions staff may make and which must return to your office.

Use three fictional demonstration cases: an ordinary service inquiry, a request that does not fit the instructions and an unavailable destination. Ask the provider to show the supported handoff and the record the office receives. These are proposed checks, not tests we performed. A lower unit total is not proof of a better customer outcome.

sections.title: Compare Revo separately and request the complete offer
paragraphs:
Revo’s current Pricing page displays a Solo launch offer of $87.50 per month with 100 included revenue-agent minutes, against a $175 list price. That is a different service and billing description, not 100 Abby Minutes or a human-receptionist entitlement. This snapshot establishes no Revo human network or named software integration.

Before choosing either provider, record answering scope, escalation ownership, the definition of usage, applicable additional charges and the written billing terms. Ask whether taxes are included in the quoted total and how a trial becomes paid service. Compare the offer that fits your workflow; this article makes no savings or performance claim.

sections.title: Separate the base charge from the usage charge
paragraphs:
The pricing page presents pay-as-you-go live answering, without a minimum usage commitment to a minute plan, and states that qualifying rates decrease automatically as usage grows. “No overage fees” does not make the variable usage charge disappear.

Treat a budget as a base component plus billable activity under the applicable rate schedule, then any other applicable charges. Ask for the actual schedule before assigning a rate to a forecast. The reviewed public page does not disclose numerical bracket thresholds or establish whether a qualifying rate applies to all usage or to separate bands.

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [AnswerFirst: current pricing](https://answerfirst.com/pricing/).

sections.title: Use seconds correctly in a conditional calculation
paragraphs:
AnswerFirst advertises one-second billing rather than rounding calls up to a full minute. The published price range is dollars per minute, not dollars per second. Preserve that distinction when building a worksheet.

Original fictional case: suppose 120 calls each produce exactly 75 billable seconds. That is 9,000 seconds, or 150 minutes. If the applicable offer used a single rate for those minutes, the following arithmetic would result. Neither endpoint is a verified bracket for 150 minutes.

| Hypothetical rate applied to the same 150 minutes | Usage arithmetic | Plus $30 base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $1.60 per minute | 150 × $1.60 = $240 | $270 |
| $1.95 per minute | 150 × $1.95 = $292.50 | $322.50 |

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [AnswerFirst: service-industry answering](https://answerfirst.com/service-providers/).

sections.title: Resolve the written terms before calling that a quote
paragraphs:
The arithmetic excludes taxes, supplemental services and other applicable charges. It also assumes the billable seconds are known. It is not a predicted invoice or a claim that every answered call produces only conversation-time charges.

The pricing FAQ says complex customization can attract a one-time fee; one forwarding number is included and additional forwarding numbers are listed at $3 monthly each. Separately, the terms refer to the Service Plan and Rate Schedule, setup and supplemental fees, applicable taxes and surcharges, and one-second usage subject to plan minimums.

Have the provider reconcile the public offer with the specific proposal you would accept. Record the answer rather than selecting whichever wording gives the lowest spreadsheet total. This review did not submit a lead form to obtain the detailed pricing packet.

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [AnswerFirst: current pricing](https://answerfirst.com/pricing/), [AnswerFirst: terms of service](https://answerfirst.com/terms-of-service/).

sections.title: Ask these questions about the rate function
paragraphs:
For a seasonal home-service office, a low-volume month and a storm-driven spike can be materially different workloads. Give the provider both scenarios using the same call-handling instructions, then request an itemized explanation.

- Which usage levels trigger each rate, and which billing period determines qualification?
- Does one qualifying rate apply to all usage, or are charges calculated across bands?
- Which activities start and stop the billable clock, including transfers and after-call work?
- Do any minimums, setup items or supplemental charges apply to this exact account?
- How are taxes and surcharges shown, and what written terms govern cancellation and the final bill?

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [AnswerFirst: terms of service](https://answerfirst.com/terms-of-service/).

sections.title: Evaluate the people and the handoff, not only the timer
paragraphs:
AnswerFirst explicitly offers live, U.S.-based receptionists for home-service businesses. For an owner who wants people answering, that is a relevant service distinction—not a reason to compare its minute directly with an AI allowance as though the purchases were identical.

Prepare an original demonstration brief with a normal inquiry, a caller changing an existing request and a failed attempt to reach your staff. Define the desired outcome for each: information captured, request assigned or supported appointment confirmed. Ask to inspect the resulting office record. These are suggested evaluation cases, not calls we placed or outcomes we observed.

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [AnswerFirst: service-industry answering](https://answerfirst.com/service-providers/), [AnswerFirst: live virtual receptionists](https://answerfirst.com/virtual-receptionist/).

sections.title: Put Revo on a separate, explicit line
paragraphs:
Revo currently lists the Crew launch offer at $175 monthly for 200 revenue-agent minutes, against a $350 list price. Its over-allowance FAQ directs customers to upgrade or discuss additional minutes; it does not publish a per-minute excess rate to fill into this comparison.

If you want an AI answering option, use the current Revo Pricing page to confirm scope and capacity. If live receptionists are a requirement, do not assume Revo supplies that human service. Choose after the provider has explained the workflow and complete bill, not from an unsupported claim of equivalence or savings.

Sources checked October 27, 2026: [Revo: current Pricing](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing).

faqs.a: No. The offer has a monthly base and usage charges. Confirm the applicable rate schedule and any additional items in the proposal.

faqs.a: No. It is per minute, with usage measured in one-second increments. A spreadsheet must convert seconds to minutes before applying a per-minute rate.

faqs.a: The reviewed page does not publish bracket thresholds or the complete calculation function. Request the rate schedule and an itemized scenario for your account.

sections.title: Read the current price card in its own units
paragraphs:
On October 27, 2026, Gabbyville’s official pricing page listed Solo at $399 per month with 50 calls included and additional calls at $7 each. It describes per-call billing without a minute cap. The same page lists Boutique at $749 for 100 calls. These are dated published figures, not a tailored quote. [Gabbyville pricing](https://www.gabbyville.com/pricing/)

Treat a call allowance as a billing unit, not a count of new customers. An existing customer can call twice about the same job. A transferred conversation, repeated caller or very short connection may also raise a counting question. Obtain the supplier’s written definition instead of deciding from the price-card heading.

sections.title: Use these original cost examples
paragraphs:
For the published Solo figures, the illustrative base calculation is $399 + $7 × calls above 50. The following fictional monthly counts assume every listed call is billable once and no other charge applies:

- 50 calls: $399 + (0 × $7) = $399.
- 75 calls: $399 + (25 × $7) = $574.
- 100 calls: $399 + (50 × $7) = $749.

sections.title: A matching total does not make two plans identical
paragraphs:
At 100 calls, that Solo calculation equals the published Boutique base price. It does not establish that the plans provide the same workflow. Compare permitted intake, routing and handoff before choosing between them. The arithmetic does not include taxes, a negotiated arrangement or any charge not established in the example.

Build two columns from your own records: the calls you expect the service to handle in an ordinary month and the calls in a plausible busy month. Keep durations as a separate column for comparison with minute-based alternatives. Do not turn an included-minute allowance from another supplier into the same number of included calls.

sections.title: Identify the live or hybrid arrangement explicitly
paragraphs:
Gabbyville markets its price-card offering as live U.S.-based reception, and separately publishes an AI-plus-live hybrid service. Its hybrid page describes AI answering with scheduling and transfers. Ask which arrangement the proposal covers, when a person receives the call and which tasks that person performs. A brand name alone does not answer those questions. [Gabbyville hybrid offering](https://www.gabbyville.com/hybrid-ai-live-receptionist/)

This distinction matters when a customer asks something beyond the approved script. Write the fallback your business wants: collect the unresolved question, reach an authorized employee or follow another agreed path. Do not describe an AI escalation as a guaranteed staffed handoff until the specific arrangement is confirmed.

sections.title: Prepare a contractor call-count and scope card
paragraphs:
Gabbyville’s home-services page specifically addresses plumbing, HVAC, electrical and other service trades. Its published examples include intake and appointment handling. That audience fit does not settle the authority you give an answering provider. [Gabbyville home services](https://www.gabbyville.com/home-services/)

Use this original card for a proposal review. Record a written answer or mark the item unresolved; an empty field is not an included feature.

- Counting: definition of a billable call, treatment of repeats, short calls, transfers and failed connections.
- Hours: intended coverage and the destination when an escalation recipient is unavailable.
- Intake: required callback details, service address and requested work; who decides job acceptance.
- Booking: permitted appointment types and the record that proves confirmation.
- Commercial terms: plan, included calls, additional-call rate, other charges and change or cancellation process.
- Record handoff: what the office receives, where it finds unresolved requests and who maintains the instructions.

sections.title: Compare Revo only for the inbound work you need
paragraphs:
Revo is an AI receptionist offer. Its current plans publish 24/7 answering, the business’s own script and rules, booking and call summaries. Crew and Fleet list transfers to the customer’s team; this is not a claim that Revo supplies a network of live receptionists. [Revo plans](/pricing)

A useful comparison follows the same fictional incoming request through both proposed setups: capture the request, explain whether a visit is merely requested or confirmed, and show the office’s next action. Compare the documented scope and billing units. This guide establishes no savings, service-quality ranking or functional equivalence between every Gabbyville and Revo feature.

Review Revo’s current plans for your inbound answering needs. Confirm your script, booking rules, required handoff and plan scope before routing calls.

sections.title: The public minute allowance needs reconciliation
paragraphs:
On October 27, the [pricing cards](https://www.phonely.ai/pricing) displayed Starter 200 and Professional 650 minutes; the comparison displayed 250 and 750 under both cycles. These observations do not establish two confirmed offers from which a buyer can freely choose.

We have not established which allowance controls a purchase. Do not silently choose the higher figure, assume the lower figure is safer, or label either section a typo. Ask which dated offer governs the account and preserve its allowance in the written proposal. Until that is settled, an effective cost per included minute or a workload-based savings comparison would rest on an unsupported input.

sections.title: Keep the billing cycle attached to every rate
paragraphs:
The cards listed monthly Starter at $50 and Professional at $150; annual monthly equivalents were $33 and $100, respectively, billed annually. An annual monthly equivalent is not the same payment arrangement as a monthly subscription. Confirm the amount due, term, renewal and applicable charges before treating that label as your invoice.

The comparison section also displayed Starter overage at $0.25 per minute for monthly billing and $0.35 for annual billing. Pro displayed $0.30 in both. Different cycle-specific labels are not automatically an error, but they cannot be swapped in a calculation. The page’s approximate call counts should not be treated as guaranteed call allowances.

sections.title: Check the work around the AI conversation
paragraphs:
Phonely’s FAQ says a transfer can leave a billable telephony connection active, with exceptions for certain arrangements. Have the provider identify the method and rate for your proposed configuration; do not assume the AI conversation ending also ends every billable leg.

For a contractor, test the proposed result as well as the billing definition. A caller may request an estimate, ask about an existing visit or need a staff member. Determine which information is recorded, which action is authorized and who receives an unresolved request. Keep a requested time separate from an appointment actually confirmed by the supported system.

sections.title: Decide who builds and maintains the agent
paragraphs:
Buildout labels differ: Free/Starter self-serve, Pro priority support, Enterprise full buildout. The FAQ assigns team-built configuration to Enterprise. Those labels do not establish that every subscription comes with a fully managed setup.

Phonely’s [official documentation](https://docs.phonely.ai/get-started/introduction) describes visual call design, routing and connections to business tools. Ask who will configure those parts for your business, test changes and maintain them when service rules change. Priority support should be defined in the proposal rather than assumed to mean that someone else owns the whole implementation.

sections.title: Use this offer-reconciliation worksheet
paragraphs:
Copy the following fields into your comparison notes. Complete them from the applicable offer and a supported demonstration. An unanswered field stays unknown; it is not a zero-cost feature or an included service.

- Offer identity: date reviewed, plan name, billing cycle and document that governs the purchase.
- Allowance: confirmed included minutes, provider answer to the card/table discrepancy and reset rules.
- Usage: excess-minute rate, rounding and whether the proposed transfer keeps a billable connection active.
- Setup: builder, test owner, support scope, required connected tools and responsibility for future changes.
- Task acceptance: service request captured, authorized booking result, unavailable-recipient fallback and follow-up owner.
- Commercial decision: unresolved questions, approved scope and the person responsible for confirming the final offer.

sections.title: Compare the inbound task, not every platform feature
paragraphs:
If your need is inbound answering for home services, compare that defined task with Revo’s current [Services](/services) and [Pricing](/pricing). A minute plan and a software platform can bundle different responsibilities. Do not infer that Revo supplies Phonely’s flow builder, arbitrary API actions, outbound campaigns or managed Enterprise buildout.

The useful decision is whether the supported arrangement handles your incoming request accurately at a cost you can establish. If an essential allowance or configuration responsibility remains unresolved, the comparison is not ready for a definitive price ranking.

If your requirement is inbound answering for a home-service business, review Revo’s current plans against the specific call-handling work you need. Confirm plan eligibility, connection and handoff before changing your live phone setup.

faqs.a: The reviewed cards and comparison disagree. This article does not select one as the purchased entitlement; obtain the applicable written offer.

faqs.a: It is labeled as billed annually. Confirm the actual payment obligation and terms rather than reading the monthly equivalent as monthly billing.

faqs.q: Can this review establish that Revo is cheaper?
faqs.a: No. A fair calculation needs confirmed allowances, usage, charges and equivalent required work. Those inputs are not all established here.

sections.title: Separate inbound answering from the broader platform
paragraphs:
Broccoli’s [official homepage](https://www.broccoli.com/) names Inbound, Outbound, Speed to Lead, QA & Coaching, and AI Chat & Scheduling. sections.title: Make the booking demonstration specific to your office
paragraphs:
The official site illustrates an inbound job booking associated with ServiceTitan. That is a vendor presentation, not proof of compatibility with your account, job types or booking rules. Ask the proposed provider to demonstrate the exact authorized action in an approved test environment.

Use a fictional request with a defined service, area and requested time. Then add an unavailable slot or a request that does not fit the business’s accepted work. Inspect what becomes a lead record, what becomes a confirmed booking and what remains with a staff owner. A natural conversation alone does not establish that the field-service record is correct.

sections.title: Ask what the additional work includes
paragraphs:
For outbound and follow-up, identify the source of the work, trigger, retry limits and stop condition. Ask how attempts, connected conversations and any required staff work are measured. This is a question about the proposed service, not authorization to contact customers or a promise that a campaign meets every applicable requirement.

For QA & Coaching, distinguish reviewing a conversation from assigning an unresolved case to a person who can act. For AI Chat & Scheduling, identify the channel, record and authorized calendar action separately from the telephone workflow. sections.title: Use this module-and-quote worksheet
paragraphs:
Create one row for each required task. The fields below form an original worksheet you can reuse with the provider and your office. “Not required” is useful: it prevents a broad platform proposal from being compared with a narrower service as though both purchases were identical.

- Required task: [incoming request / supported booking / outbound follow-up / source response / call review / website conversation].
- Proposed scope: [named Broccoli module or written offer reference; included, excluded or unresolved].
- Authorized action: [record to create or change, applicable business rule and responsible owner].
- Acceptance evidence: [approved test case, observed result and unresolved exception].
- Implementation: [setup owner, prerequisites, staff work and future change responsibility].
- Commercial terms: [billing unit, allowance, recurring amount, one-time amount and excess-usage rule from the actual offer].

sections.title: Keep implementation and ongoing ownership visible
paragraphs:
Ask who maintains the script, business knowledge, staff destinations and service rules after launch. If several locations or teams are involved, identify who approves changes and how an unavailable recipient is handled. A corrected operating rule should not depend on an informal promise that nobody owns.

Have the provider identify any relevant implementation work, recurring administration or usage conditions in writing. These are questions to resolve, not verified fee categories. We have not established a universal minimum, contract length, setup charge or onboarding duration for a Broccoli purchase.

sections.title: Use a narrower comparison when that is the real need
paragraphs:
Revo’s published [Services](/services) and [Pricing](/pricing) are relevant when the requirement is its supported inbound-answering, booking and handoff work. They do not establish an equivalent to Broccoli’s entire platform, outbound operation, QA/coaching or field-service actions.

Compare the required incoming-call outcome first. If the broader modules are necessary, keep them in a separate scope rather than declaring a phone-only offer a complete substitute. Without an applicable Broccoli price and matched responsibilities, this review cannot responsibly calculate a savings percentage or call either option the cheaper purchase.

If your requirement is inbound answering for a home-service business, review Revo’s current plans against the specific call-handling work you need. Confirm plan eligibility, connection and handoff before changing your live phone setup.

faqs.q: Does Broccoli publish a fixed starting price?

sections.title: What Posh currently offers
paragraphs:
[Posh’s current AI page](https://posh.com/ai/) describes a combination of AI answering and live receptionists. Callers can move from AI to a human, with transfer rules configured during setup. The page specifically discusses home-service lead qualification and human handling of escalations. Those are vendor descriptions, not performance results established by our review.

sections.title: What selected customers reported
paragraphs:
The [Posh Trustpilot profile](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/posh.com) supplies identifiable examples, rather than proof of typical results. Rocky Mountain Exteriors, in a review posted June 6, 2025 about a May 24 experience, reported helpful after-hours handling and account support. The Professor Law Firm reported smooth setup on September 14, 2026; its legal-office context differs from a contractor’s dispatch workflow.

There is criticism too. Posh Event Center’s April 12, 2026 review, describing an October 25, 2025 experience, reported unexpectedly high costs and more calls reaching the business than anticipated, while valuing human answering. Posh replied that transfer attempts could relate to setup. That explanation is the vendor’s response, not an independently established cause.

Trustpilot labels these reports Verified. We have not authenticated them ourselves. These selected accounts are not a representative sample or a customer consensus, and older live-service experiences do not prove the quality of today’s AI offering.

sections.title: Read the billing units before comparing monthly prices
paragraphs:
Posh’s AI page describes plans with a shared allowance of AI and live receptionist minutes, followed by different overage rates for each. Its billing explanation also includes immediate follow-up tasks. A call that uses AI and then a human can incur both types of overage after the allowance is exhausted. Check the current terms directly before buying.

Build a scenario from your own records instead of comparing starting prices alone. Use a typical month and a busy month. Write down answered-call minutes, minutes transferred to humans, follow-up work and any other quoted charges. Ask the provider to calculate both scenarios in writing and explain how usage appears on the invoice.

sections.title: Use this call-handling worksheet in your evaluation
paragraphs:
Copy these five scenarios into your evaluation notes. For each, record the expected action, actual result, minutes used and correction needed:

1. **New customer outside your service area.** Supply a ZIP code you do not serve. The expected result is an accurate explanation and your chosen next step, without an unsupported appointment promise.
2. **Routine appointment request.** Give a real type of job but use a fictional caller. Record whether the result is a message, appointment request or confirmed booking, and what makes that status clear.
3. **Existing customer asking for an update.** Specify what information the answering service may access and what must go to your office. Check that it does not guess an arrival time.
4. **Caller requesting a person.** Document the handoff destination, hours, information passed along and fallback when nobody answers. Include the cost of that path.
5. **Urgent-sounding request after hours.** Use a hypothetical scenario agreed with the provider. Check your escalation instructions and fallback; do not assume an answering service replaces emergency services.

Use the same scenarios for every shortlisted service. Arrange a demonstration or controlled evaluation with permission, rather than sending fake emergencies through a live customer queue. Keep personal customer information out of evaluation material.

sections.title: Questions to settle before you choose
paragraphs:
Ask who maintains your instructions and how quickly changes take effect. Establish how you report an incorrect message or transfer and how the provider confirms the correction. Request the cancellation terms and treatment of unused allowances. Decide which failures would stop the evaluation: an appointment promised without authorization, an incorrect service-area decision or an escalation sent to the wrong person.

Posh merits consideration when you want to evaluate a documented AI-plus-human model. Your decision should rest on the agreed call flow, observed evaluation results and written costs. If you are also considering Revo, compare its documented plan scope separately; this guide does not establish equivalent human staffing or transfer arrangements.

Review its published scope alongside your other options.

faqs.q: Do Posh reviews establish how its AI receptionist performs?
faqs.a: Not by themselves. A report may concern live answering, onboarding or an older configuration. Ask which service was used and evaluate the current call flow against your own requirements.

faqs.q: What should a home-service business compare first?
faqs.a: Start with intake accuracy, booking authority and escalation destination. Then price the same typical and busy-month scenarios across providers.

# Posh Virtual Receptionist Reviews: A Buyer’s Checklist

Looking at Posh virtual receptionist reviews? Separate the current offer, the experience reported by an individual customer and the workflow your business needs before choosing an answering service.

## How this review was prepared

Revo publishes this review and sells a competing AI answering service. We reviewed public Posh product information and selected customer reports on Trustpilot on October 27, 2026. We did not purchase Posh, place test calls or independently verify reviewers’ experiences. This is a documentary buying guide, without a Revo-assigned score or claim to independent product testing.

The useful question is whether the service can handle your particular calls at an acceptable cost. A favorable review from another business cannot settle your service-area rules, scheduling requirements or escalation instructions.

## What Posh currently offers

[Posh’s current AI page](https://posh.com/ai/) describes a combination of AI answering and live receptionists. Callers can move from AI to a human, with transfer rules configured during setup. The page specifically discusses home-service lead qualification and human handling of escalations. Those are vendor descriptions, not performance results established by our review.

That distinction matters when comparing providers. Confirm who receives an escalated call: your employee, a provider’s receptionist or another destination. Do not treat those arrangements as interchangeable. If a human answering team is essential, request an explicit explanation of its availability and responsibilities.

## What selected customers reported

The [Posh Trustpilot profile](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/posh.com) supplies identifiable examples, rather than proof of typical results. Rocky Mountain Exteriors, in a review posted June 6, 2025 about a May 24 experience, reported helpful after-hours handling and account support. The Professor Law Firm reported smooth setup on September 14, 2026; its legal-office context differs from a contractor’s dispatch workflow.

There is criticism too. Posh Event Center’s April 12, 2026 review, describing an October 25, 2025 experience, reported unexpectedly high costs and more calls reaching the business than anticipated, while valuing human answering. Posh replied that transfer attempts could relate to setup. That explanation is the vendor’s response, not an independently established cause.

Trustpilot labels these reports Verified. We have not authenticated them ourselves. These selected accounts are not a representative sample or a customer consensus, and older live-service experiences do not prove the quality of today’s AI offering.

## Read the billing units before comparing monthly prices

Posh’s AI page describes plans with a shared allowance of AI and live receptionist minutes, followed by different overage rates for each. Its billing explanation also includes immediate follow-up tasks. A call that uses AI and then a human can incur both types of overage after the allowance is exhausted. Check the current terms directly before buying.

Build a scenario from your own records instead of comparing starting prices alone. Use a typical month and a busy month. Write down answered-call minutes, minutes transferred to humans, follow-up work and any other quoted charges. Ask the provider to calculate both scenarios in writing and explain how usage appears on the invoice.

## Use this call-handling worksheet in your evaluation

Copy these five scenarios into your evaluation notes. For each, record the expected action, actual result, minutes used and correction needed:

1. **New customer outside your service area.** Supply a ZIP code you do not serve. The expected result is an accurate explanation and your chosen next step, without an unsupported appointment promise.
2. **Routine appointment request.** Give a real type of job but use a fictional caller. Record whether the result is a message, appointment request or confirmed booking, and what makes that status clear.
3. **Existing customer asking for an update.** Specify what information the answering service may access and what must go to your office. Check that it does not guess an arrival time.
4. **Caller requesting a person.** Document the handoff destination, hours, information passed along and fallback when nobody answers. Include the cost of that path.
5. **Urgent-sounding request after hours.** Use a hypothetical scenario agreed with the provider. Check your escalation instructions and fallback; do not assume an answering service replaces emergency services.

Use the same scenarios for every shortlisted service. Arrange a demonstration or controlled evaluation with permission, rather than sending fake emergencies through a live customer queue. Keep personal customer information out of evaluation material.

## Questions to settle before you choose

Ask who maintains your instructions and how quickly changes take effect. Establish how you report an incorrect message or transfer and how the provider confirms the correction. Request the cancellation terms and treatment of unused allowances. Decide which failures would stop the evaluation: an appointment promised without authorization, an incorrect service-area decision or an escalation sent to the wrong person.

Posh merits consideration when you want to evaluate a documented AI-plus-human model. Your decision should rest on the agreed call flow, observed evaluation results and written costs. If you are also considering Revo, compare its documented plan scope separately; this guide does not establish equivalent human staffing or transfer arrangements.

Review its published scope alongside your other options.
